title: Embedded Engineer Roadmap
summary: Build from electronics and programming fundamentals into microcontrollers, embedded C/C++, RTOS, communication protocols, debugging and embedded product development.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a four-year B.Tech/B.E. from 2026–2030. If a four-year honours/research pathway is available, use the additional depth for embedded systems research, real-time operating systems, automotive electronics, IoT or hardware-software co-design.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build electronics, C/C++, microcontrollers, communication protocols, debugging and embedded project skills.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Move into firmware, RTOS, automotive embedded, IoT, embedded Linux, hardware validation or device engineering.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward senior embedded, firmware, systems or embedded architecture responsibilities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine embedded systems with edge AI, cybersecurity, real-time computing, advanced SoCs and connected devices.

rows.text: C programming, digital electronics, circuit fundamentals
Microprocessors, microcontrollers and basic electronics interfacing
GPIO, LED, button and timer projects
Embedded C, interrupts, timers, ADC/DAC, PWM
UART, SPI, I2C, CAN and debugging
Embedded Linux, device drivers and networking

blocks.text: 4-year honours variant
Use the additional academic depth for embedded Linux, RTOS, automotive systems, FPGA/SoC development, robotics, edge AI, IoT security or embedded systems research.

rows.text: MCU, sensors, MQTT, connectivity, edge computing

blocks.text: Continue into heterogeneous SoCs, edge AI, embedded cybersecurity, real-time AI, automotive software, robotics, industrial control, connected devices and hardware-software co-design.
